British Values
British Values at St Stephen’ C of E Primary school.
Promoting British Values
At St Stephen’s Primary School, we reflect, celebrate and respect our rich and diverse community through our curriculum, our Christian values and ethos, and composite school activities. We give voice to our community, made up of a wide range of culture, faiths and ethnicity through the exploration of specific subjects and events as shown in our school curriculum. We strongly believe in the rule of law and expose our children to the British values of:
This was emphasized in the June 2014, by the DfES while stating the following: “all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”

Register of Interests
Governors and staff members who regularly attend meetings of the governing body and its committees must declare any business or personal interest that might influence any decision they may make especially in financial matters. Any governor with such an interest must declare it annually and notify the school of any changes that occur. Where there is a conflict of interest the governor must withdraw from the meeting and take no part in the discussions or vote. The agenda of each meeting requires governors and non-governors present to declare any interest they may have in any of the items to be discussed.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Stephen's Church of England Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Collective Worship is an integral part of St. Stephen’s C of E Primary School.
Our pupils participate in Collective Worship every day learning about stories from the Bibles and studying in depth the Christian Values.
We have close links to our local Church, St. Stephen’s, where we celebrate key dates throughout the year such as Christmas, Easter and the Leaver’s performance.
At St. Stephen’s Collective worship is a daily event and is central to the life of the school. Collective worship makes a major contribution to upholding the religious character and Christian distinctiveness of a church school. We see Collective Worship as an important opportunity to provide pupils with spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. Collective worship, at St. Stephen’s, is integral to our ethos, vision and mission statement. We seek to develop the children’s respect for and understanding of Christianity, to understand Anglican traditions and practice and to give them awareness of other faiths and festivals. St. Stephen’s has an established relationship with the clergy of the local church.
In St Stephen’s our Christian vision shapes all we do.
As an inclusive, Christian school, we will nurture, inspire, empower and expect every child to achieve their very best in life, work and the community.
‘Collective Worship in a Church school should enable every child and adult to flourish and to live life in all its fullness. (John 10:10). It will help educate for wisdom, knowledge and skills, hope and aspiration, dignity and respect, and developing community and understanding of living well together.
This year children, in Collective Worship, will learn in depth about 6 Christian values:
Shown on the right are a few display boards pupils created showing three Christian Values.
Collective worship provides a distinct, calm space away from the busy school day. These times ofworship, prayer and reflection are effective in drawing together the school community to focus onspiritual growth

St Stephens Church
St Stephen's, South Lambeth is an inner city church
The church membership reflects the diversity of the local community. Our morning services are lively, child-friendly and relaxed.
They include age-specific groups for the children and teenagers. Our part-time youth Pastor leads the work with our teenagers.
The London branch of Fegans Child & Family Care is based at St Stephen's. A team of trained workers offers help and support to children and families in the community around North Lambeth.
The church has a number of midweek 'Growth Groups' meeting in church and homes enabling members to put their growing Christian faith into practice in their everyday lives. Fegans run a group for parents with young children on Thursday mornings.
To find out more about our Sunday Services visit our website.
10:30 am Sunday Service
Everyone is welcome to join us and worship Jesus. The refreshments are also warm and welcoming!
St Stephen's Church provide a crèche & Sunday School
St Stephen's benefits from very strong links with the local church and children's centre and this positive and powerful partnership further extends the distinctive Christian character of the school.”

pageCache.text:
VISION CURRICULUM GOALS, 3I's
EYFS Curriculum
Nursery and Reception
Intent
At St Stephen’s, our aim is to create a learning environment and build relationships which support, enhance and invite a child’s curiosity, confidence and individual competency to flourish regardless of backgrounds, circumstances or needs. We aim to work collaboratively with parents and carers to encourage independent, enthusiastic learners who thrive and reach their full potential. It is our intent that children who enter our EYFS begin their lifelong learning journey by developing physically, verbally, cognitively and emotionally whilst also embedding a positive attitude to school and a love of learning.
To ensure children make outstanding progress, it is our intent to take into consideration their starting points and needs of our pupils as they begin their learning journey. Every child has access to a broad, balanced and adapted curriculum which prepares them for now and for the future in terms of opportunities and experiences. Following personal interests and individual needs, allows us to plan and provide indoor and outdoor opportunities, throughout our EYFS curriculum to support learning and development and achieve their next steps.
Our EYFS curriculum aims to enable our children to be:
Competent and creative learners; who are curious about the world around them.
Secure and confident; who enjoy coming to school and learning new skills and knowledge building on their existing learning.
Skilful communicators; who connect with others through language and play, ensuring that they play in a vocab rich environment.
It is our intent to ensure that all children will receive the teaching of early reading through systematic, synthetic phonics (Read, Write Inc.) to learn to read words and simple sentences accurately by the end of Reception.
We work to build a strong partnership with parents and carer, through termly workshops.
Implementation
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage framework. This is made up of four overriding principles which our early year’s education is based upon:
The curriculum provides a play-based learning environment, combined with focused teaching and basic skills, to ensure children make rapid progress before moving onto Year 1. The children in both Nursery and Reception are provided with ample opportunities accessible in our indoor and outdoor provision. They engage in planned, focussed activities as well as self-initiated and free flow activities. The learning experiences within our Early Years are linked to the seven areas of learning and development within the EYFS. These areas are split into three prime areas and four specific areas. The three prime areas are those which the children should develop first and are considered most essential for the healthy development and future learning of our children. These include:
As children grow and make progress in the prime areas, this will help them to naturally develop skills within the four specific areas. These are:
Children benefit from meaningful learning across the curriculum and staff plan resourcefully for opportunities for communication, sustained shared thinking and physical challenge to build on existing skills taking into account the Characteristics of Effective Learning.
Rich first hand experiences (inside, outdoors, visitors and school trips) to widen experiences, awe and wonderment. Exploratory learning and thinking creatively including problem solving across all areas of learning. New vocabulary and concepts through reading will excite and engage all learners which includes staff modelling standard English and asking high quality questions.
Impact
Our children grow to be confident, competent lifelong learners and good citizens not just in the school community, but the wider community.
The children at St Stephen’s experience a smooth transition between Nursery, Reception and beyond. Effective communication and collaboration ensure the children leave the EYFS with a solid foundation of learning of which to build upon entering into Key stage one.
We use online learning journals and Floor books across the EYFS, supplemented with exercise books in Reception, which evidence to the children and their families the successes of the children throughout their time in Early Years.
Assessment impacts are moderated internally and externally.
From their own starting point children will make progress academically and socially so that they are prepared for Key stage 1.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Stephen's Church of England Primary School - Nursery and Reception
pageCache.text:
Nursery and Reception
At St Stephen’s we aim to provide our children with the foundation they need to thrive in life. We believe our children learn best in a stimulating and engaging environment. Through inquiry-based learning and play, our curriculum aims to engage and stimulate young children and nurture their academic, personal and social development.
We are committed to each child making progress and we provide a wide range of activities that enable the children to become independent learners, who are willing to take risks.
The resources and materials available to the children are of a high quality, open-ended, well-ordered and accessible to the children. They are carefully selected for their potential to promote learning and sustained high-level involvement. Resources and contexts are available which motivate the children to explore and problem solve, play imaginatively and make representations (to paint, draw, create models, dance and make music). These opportunities are available in the indoor and outdoor environments.
We extend our classroom provision with a range of interesting trips and out of school activities throughout the year. We also arrange for school visiting specialists and resources to enrich the curriculum.
We work closely with our parents and carers as we understand the importance of parent support in their child’s learning. We offer regular coffee mornings, which help support parents with the different areas of the curriculum and parents have the opportunity for ‘stay and play sessions in the EYFS. This gives parents the opportunity to engage with their children during the school day and see how their child is developing at school.
You are welcome to attend the School for a school visit.
Contact the school office to arrange a suitable time.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Stephen's Church of England Primary School - Behaviour System
pageCache.text:
Behaviour Centre
We actively promote and reward good behaviour.
Our new certificate awards system has been popular amongst both the staff and pupils. This is how it works.
At the start of the year every pupil received a bronze stamp chart. Once a pupil has completed their charts, they will be awarded with a certificate. A pupil will be awarded with a bronze certificate and star badge during Monday’s certificate assembly after completing 3 stamp charts.
The pupil will then progress to the silver stage and the same process continues at this stage.
Once the student has completed 3 silver stamp charts they will progress onto the GOLD stage. And then the whole process starts again!
There is a very strong community ethos in the school and local charitable organisations benefit from this sense of mission. Pupils also understand their responsibility to the wider world and, during a term in which they focused on the Christian value of compassion, they recently donated resources to a grateful primary school in Ghana.
Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools Report, Dec '16
